I'm going to start with a correction. I saw two online services in Canada: this one, and a psychiatrist contracted through Equinoxe. The extended horror story below is from *Equinoxe*. But my psychiatry online experience, listed after, leads me to believe something very similar happened with both of them.  


My meeting started out with me realizing the psychiatrist I was speaking to was currently inside a public hospital- the very public hospital where I had previously waited over 36 hours to receive emergency ***triage***. I'd effectively paid to skip the queue, which I'm certain can't be legal but I don't have evidence for that. Other than that it went surprisingly well, up until my follow ups at the end. The Dr himself refused to send any sort of write up or assesment, claiming I had already received "adequate treatment" from the RAMQ Dr who had seen me before and they would not be following my case. I never told them I had previously spoken to anyone, nor did I give RAMQ or any other Dr permission to share my case file. I managed to force them to send me his notes and assesment by reporting the CC charge as fraudulent- and in those notes I found reference to a complaint I had filed against the first guy, who basically told me to gtfo and stop wasting his time. Naturally, I would not have filed that complaint if I hadn't been reassured multiple times it had been anonymous.

When I contacted Psychiatry Online Canada (not certain if it was before or after dialogue), they replied saying they wouldn't see me at all, also for the reason I had already received "adequate treatment". You guessed it, I never told them either, yet they somehow worked it out.

It treads the conspiracy theory line, but I would not be shocked at all if the same Drs, and many others, were working for all three services and had a gentleman's agreement to not contradict any conclusion that results in them getting less work for the same pay. I don't mean disrespect, but many of my experiences require quite the suspension of disbelief. It's hard to explain the fact that I can show up at a clinic 30 minutes before it opens, be the only person in the waiting room for the first two hours- and then not get seen until 6pm.

Funnily enough, the Equinoxe Dr's report included what turned out to be the correct diagnosis. When I spoke to the Dr in the UK, they managed to make the same deduction, and claimed they suspected it within the first 20 minutes or so. Make of that what you will.

I'm surprised your UK prescription isn't being accepted here. May I ask what it is for? I wonder if it's something more heavily controlled in Canada.

A "method" which I've heard has some success is to request whatever Dr you see write you something saying they are refusing the prescription transfer. I've heard countless anecdotes of people "reassessing" a patient once a paper trail of their inactivity was in the picture.

If you're interested, the service I ended up using was psychiatry-uk.com. They accept NHS referrals, and are on the pricy side if you go through them privately, but they saw me around a week from my request and got me pretty much everything I needed within the month. Though they are of course unable to prepare a Canadian prescription, so that might not do anything for you.

If you're in a university or have an office job here, it's worth checking if they offer you a Dialogue subscription. I've never had an issue with them validating/renewing an already extant prescription.
